title: Jollof Rice
subtitle: West African one-pot rice cooked in spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: Jollof rice is the most celebrated dish in West Africa. Rice is cooked directly in a rich blended tomato and pepper base until it absorbs all the colour and flavour of the sauce. Every country has its own version, and the debate over whose is best never ends.
sourceNotes: Jollof rice takes its name from the Jolof Empire of Senegal, which flourished from the 14th to 16th centuries. From there it spread across West Africa. Today, Ghana and Nigeria in particular each claim the best version -- the debate over Ghanaian versus Nigerian jollof is one of the great friendly disputes of West African culture.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales up well. Use a wider pot to maintain the correct ratio of surface area to depth.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato base can be made 2 days ahead.

content.text: The smoky, slightly charred bottom layer of rice -- called party jollof -- is a badge of honour in West Africa. To get it, cook the rice on medium heat for the last few minutes without stirring. This is not burning -- it is the goal.

items.prepNote: 1 roughly chopped for the base, 1 finely sliced for frying

content.text: Blend the tinned tomatoes, red peppers, and 1 roughly chopped onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the sliced onion for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes.

Pour in the blended tomato base. Add the tomato puree, allspice, bay leaves, and salt. Fry the paste over medium-high heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens in colour and the oil separates on the surface.
Pour in the stock. Bring to the boil. Add the rinsed rice and stir to combine.
Reduce heat to very low. Cover tightly with foil and then the lid. Cook for 25 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove the foil and lid. If the rice is cooked and no liquid remains, turn the heat to medium for 2 to 3 minutes to develop the smoky bottom layer. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Rice is raw in the middle
items.cause: Lid lifted too early or heat too low
items.fix: Do not lift the lid during cooking; if rice is still raw, add 100ml of hot water and cover for another 10 minutes

items.cause: Too much liquid or not rinsed properly
items.fix: Rinse rice thoroughly before use and measure the stock carefully
Fry the blended tomato paste until it is very thick, dark, and the oil has separated -- at least 15 minutes

content.text: Jollof rice is eaten at every celebration, funeral, wedding, and party across West Africa. It is served in Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and beyond. Each country insists its own version is the original and the best. The debate is affectionate and endless. What all versions share is the technique of cooking the rice inside the sauce.
